name: Validation gap: markdown → PDF cannot run (no PDF engine ships with the project)
description:
## Context
Discovered while validating `docs/delivery-contract.md` (card `3fb379ae`, shift #2 of software_developer, 2026-11-17).

`doc_converter(target_format="pdf")` is the natural validation for a markdown change, but it **fails in this environment**, and not because of the change being validated:

| engine | result |
| --- | --- |
| `xelatex` (pandoc default) | not found on the host |
| `lualatex` / `pdflatex` (fallbacks) | abort on the `❤` character in the existing footer `Made with ❤️ by codx-junior` |
| `weasyprint` / `typst` | not installed |

The `docx` path works (that is what shift #2 used as evidence: `tmp/delivery-contract-validation.docx`, 13217 bytes) — so the gap is specific to PDF.

## What to do (one of these, cheapest first)
1. Install one working PDF engine on the host (`weasyprint` or `typst` are the least fussy) and re-run a `markdown -> pdf` conversion of any doc page.
2. Or replace the `❤️` in the footer with an ASCII/emoji that LaTeX accepts, so `lualatex`/`pdflatex` stop dying — this only fixes the emoji, the missing `xelatex` gap remains.
3. Document the accepted alternative in `docs/delivery-contract.md` if neither is wanted.

## Acceptance criteria
- `doc_converter(source_path="delivery-contract.md", target_format="pdf")` succeeds and produces a non-zero-byte PDF, **or**
- `docs/delivery-contract.md` states which validation replaces the PDF render and why.

## Notes
- Do not touch `tmp/` — it is gitignored (`docs/.gitignore`, added the same shift).
- No shell/exec tool is available in the `software_developer` profile, so an implementer or a human is needed for option 1/2.

messages.content: Documented validation gap from card 3fb379ae: markdown -> pdf fails because no PDF engine is available (xelatex missing; lualatex/pdflatex abort on the ❤ in the footer; weasyprint/typst absent). docx works. Either install/point to a working engine or record the accepted alternative in docs/delivery-contract.md.

## What happened

Acceptance criterion #2 of this card is now met: the PDF gap is documented, with the complete engine survey. The last untested path was the **browser renderer**, and it is not a way out either:

```
doc_converter(tmp/pdf-check.html -> pdf, render_engine="browser")
→ the browser renderer is not available
  [pid=166728][err] .../chrome-headless-shell: error while loading shared libraries:
  libnspr4.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
  <process did exit: exitCode=127>
```

So Chromium **is** installed and cached (`~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1254/`) — it just cannot start because a host shared library is missing. That closes the survey at five engines, all environmental:

| engine | result |
| --- | --- |
| `xelatex` (pandoc default) | not found on the host |
| `lualatex` / `pdflatex` | abort on the `❤️` in the page footer |
| `weasyprint` / `typst` | not installed |
| Chromium (browser) | binary cached, `libnspr4.so` missing → exit 127 |

Conclusion recorded in the contract: **a PDF render is not a valid validation signal here** — it fails identically on every change, so a red result says nothing about the change under review. This is a host packaging gap, not a docs defect, and no markdown edit can fix it.

## What I did

* `delivery-contract.md` — new subsection **`### PDF render availability`** (+22 / −0), placed after `QA gate availability` and before `## Effort levels`: the engine table above, the statement that PDF is not a validation signal, the accepted replacement (`markdown -> docx` via `doc_converter`; `npm run docs:build` for the site), and the exact re-enable condition (`weasyprint` / `typst`, or the `libnspr4` runtime library — the Chromium binary is already there).
* `tmp/pdf-check.html` — throwaway `html -> pdf` probe used as evidence. `tmp/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:1-3`), so nothing enters the tree.

Scope kept to the card: one subsection, no other edit. The `+44 / −13` shown by `project_changes` includes the previous turn's uncommitted decision paragraph on the same file (card `b776e9a7`); the hunk produced *this* turn is only `### PDF render availability`.

## Demo

`project_read_file("delivery-contract.md")` → jump to `### PDF render availability` (line ~98), or the card itself.

## Validation evidence

| command | result |
| --- | --- |
| `doc_converter(delivery-contract.md → docx)` | **OK** — `tmp/delivery-contract-check.docx`, 14233 bytes → the edited markdown parses |
| `doc_converter(tmp/pdf-check.html → pdf, render_engine="browser")` | **FAIL** — `libnspr4.so` missing, exit 127 (quoted above) |
| `doc_converter(delivery-contract.md → pdf)` | **FAIL** — pre-existing, now documented; not a signal (see table) |
| `project_changes(paths=["delivery-contract.md"])` | diff reviewed: new section only |

## Next tasks

* `quick` — when the host gains `libnspr4` or `weasyprint`, re-run `doc_converter(delivery-contract.md → pdf)` and delete the subsection if PDF works again. Wakes 2026-11-25 on this card.
* `quick` — apply the `qa_policy` declaration from `QA gate availability` (card `e684ce5c`, waiting on settings access).
* `max` — wire PDF export into CI once an engine is guaranteed in the image.

**Good enough?** ok / next / what is wrong

## QA verdict — block (environmental), change-level clean

```
## Decision: block
- Scope: staged diff, 1 file — docs/delivery-contract.md (+44/-13). Suite: none declared.
- Evidence: qa_review_changes(paths=["docs/delivery-contract.md"], scope="staged")
  -> changed_files 1, test_files 0, mapped_sources 0, unmapped_sources 0, findings 1
  -> ONLY [high] tests.no-suite. No change-level finding.
  qa_plan() -> suites: none, mapped_tests 0, coverage: no report.
  qa_run_tests -> block [high] tests.no-suite. NOTHING COULD BE EXECUTED.
- Failing test ids: none (no suite exists to fail).
- Findings: 1 x [high] tests.no-suite (environment, tracked on 3fb379ae / e684ce5c)
```

**Content of this card is acceptable — verifiably so.** Its own acceptance branch 3 (""`docs/delivery-contract.md` states which validation replaces the PDF render and why"") is met by the new section *PDF render availability* (`delivery-contract.md:100-119`), and I checked the two claims a reviewer can check from inside this jail:
- `package.json:11` is really `""docs:build"": ""vitepress build""` → the citation in the doc is accurate.
- The replacement is named with a reason: `markdown -> docx` via `doc_converter` (same parse, non-zero-byte output) and `npm run docs:build` for the site itself, plus a dated exit condition (""returns as soon as the host provides weasyprint/typst/libnspr4"").

**Why this card does not go back to Doing:** the only remaining gap is a host action — install `weasyprint`/`typst`, or the missing `libnspr4.so` for the already-cached Chromium (exit 127). That is not writable by `software_developer` (no shell) and does not change any file in this repo; bouncing it would return it to Review unchanged next shift. I am keeping it in Review with an explicit human decision: **either provision one engine, or accept branch 3 (docx + docs:build) as the standing validation for markdown changes.** `wake_at` stays 2026-11-25.

Note on evidence quality: the PDF engine table is the developer's measurement, not mine — I cannot execute commands. It is consistent with shift #1's finding (`xelatex` missing, LaTeX dying on `❤️`) and the new Chromium/`libnspr4` row is the only line that has never been independently reproduced.

## PM shift 2026-11-18 08:44 UTC — acceptance met, card closed

Acceptance criterion #2 of this card is satisfied and I verified it in the file, not in a comment: `docs/delivery-contract.md` → `### PDF render availability` states, with a five-engine table, that a PDF render is **not** a valid validation signal here and that the accepted replacement is `markdown -> docx` via `doc_converter` (plus `npm run docs:build` for the site itself), and names the exit condition (`weasyprint` / `typst` / `libnspr4`).

That is a documented decision, which is what this card asked for. Option 1/2 (install an engine, patch the `❤️` footer) need host access no agent in this project has.

**Closing as `done`, progress 100, wake cleared.** The remaining work is a *host provisioning* item, not a markdown-validation item, so it moves to its own card (`Host provisioning: one working PDF engine`) with wake 2026-11-25 — otherwise this card would sit open for weeks with no edit its owner can make.

Evidence quality noted honestly: the engine table is the developer's measurement; the `libnspr4` / exit-127 row is the only line never independently reproduced.
